notes: A passing answer may use any sound grouping design (data classes, named tuples, small config objects); no rubric requires reproducing the names, signatures or code shape of a particular reference repair. The selected task prompt is prompt_natural.md.

rubrics.criterion: The dataset-loading function consumes the dataset identity and distribution facts - the dataset name, the user count and the IID/unequal policy - together through one cohesive grouping object instead of re-listing them as individual parameters in its signature.
rubrics.rationale: This repository's data entry point currently names the four facts individually alongside the load directory; the task prompt's first grouping role is exactly these facts, so the loader boundary is the primary place a repair must demonstrate a real grouping rather than renamed parameters.

rubrics.criterion: The startup report helper receives the facts it prints - including the dataset facts and the local-training facts - through the grouping objects rather than as a long list of individual setting parameters, while its printed output keeps reporting every fact it reports today (dataset, model, optimizer, learning rate, global rounds, IID/Non-IID, user count, fraction of users, local batch size, local epochs).
rubrics.rationale: The report is the widest declaration in this instance (ten individual setting parameters at the starting state), and it is the boundary where the dataset group and the training group meet; a repair that groups the rest of the pipeline but leaves the report's signature exploded misses the most visible participant.

rubrics.criterion: The per-user local trainer is constructed with all six of its local-training settings - batch size, local epochs, learning rate, optimizer choice, verbosity and device - carried by a single grouped object, rather than each setting being a separate constructor parameter.
rubrics.rationale: The trainer's constructor is the central consumer of the local-training group in this codebase and receives the most knobs; grouping here is the core semantic move the task prompt requests, and it is where a solver's design choice for the training context must become visible.

rubrics.criterion: Each of the three convolutional architectures receives its shape settings (channel count, filter/feature settings and class count) as one grouped object instead of three individually named constructor parameters.
rubrics.rationale: All three convolutional constructors in the starting state spell out the identical three-name shape list, even where the class ignores members; the prompt's model-shape role covers exactly these constructors, so the shape group must be applied to all three rather than one.

rubrics.criterion: No production call site still forwards one of the settings groups member-by-member: every call that previously enumerated a group's individual setting names (the loader call, the report call, the trainer constructions inside and outside the training loop, the convolutional constructions, in both experiment entry points) now passes the corresponding grouping object instead.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's maintenance burden was largely created at the call sites, where both experiment scripts hand-assemble every exploded list at each call; a repair that only changes definitions but re-lists members at calls keeps the burden the task asks to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The trainer's loader-slicing method no longer re-declares local-training members as its own parameters: the batch size it needs comes from the same training context the trainer itself holds, while the dataset and index subset remain explicit inputs.
rubrics.rationale: The slicing step repeats a subset of its own object's parameters, which is how the repeated group propagates inward in this instance; the prompt explicitly includes the trainer and its loader slicing, so a repair that leaves the method declaring (dataset, index subset, local batch size) individually is incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: The learning rate and optimizer choice reach the shared optimizer construction from the run's training-settings grouping (the grouping itself, or members read off it at a single construction site per experiment), so the trainer and the plain baseline both build their optimizer from one canonical source of those settings.
rubrics.rationale: The optimizer helper is a derived consumer of only two of the six training settings in this instance; a full repair routes these two through the same training context as everything else, but because the helper legitimately consumes a subset, a minimal sound repair may extract the members in one place - this item grades that consistency rather than a specific signature.

rubrics.criterion: The held-out evaluation pass resolves its device from the training settings grouping (or a value derived from that grouping), not from a separately threaded bare flag disconnected from the grouped pipeline, and it still evaluates on the same device it would use today.
rubrics.rationale: The evaluation function is the last consumer of the device setting in the starting state and the only one outside the trainer in each entry point; because a lone setting is not itself a repeated group, this item grades pipeline consistency for the grouping design rather than being strictly required by the repeated-pattern rule.

rubrics.criterion: No stale per-setting copies remain alongside the new groupings: in particular the local trainer does not mirror each grouping member into a separate instance attribute (self.<member> fields for every setting) when the grouped object already carries them; a value derived from a grouping (such as a device string computed from the device setting) is not such a copy.
rubrics.rationale: The starting state stores six separate self-fields on the trainer as the residue of its explanatory evolution; leaving them next to a grouping recreates the duplication the task is about, and graders need an explicit fact separating genuine derived values from wholesale member mirroring.

rubrics.criterion: No production boundary remains that still accepts or re-creates the exploded member lists: no compatibility wrapper signature still enumerates the individual setting names only to forward them into a grouping, and no experiment entry point retains a hand-assembled member-by-member argument list for a whole group.
rubrics.rationale: Partial repairs often leave behind forwarding shims or keep one old-style call for convenience; in this instance the exploding style is the artifact being retired, so any surviving member-by-member boundary (definition or call) means the cleanup half of the task was skipped.

rubrics.criterion: Dataset routing changed: a dataset name other than mnist or cifar no longer loads plain MNIST data through the fmnist directory, or the CIFAR variant changed its source dataset or normalization pipeline.
rubrics.rationale: The loader's directory selection was moved out to the callers during the evolution that created this instance, and its handling of unrecognized names is a pre-existing quirk the task explicitly pins; regrouping settings must not 'fix' that routing, and graders need to catch a well-meening cleanup that silently does.

rubrics.criterion: The local data split changed: the train/validation/test index proportions are no longer the first 80%, next 10% and last 10% of the incoming indices in order, or the train loader lost its batched shuffled configuration (with the local batch setting) or the validation/test loaders lost their computed batch sizing.
rubrics.rationale: The batch size is the setting that crosses into the trainer's slicing step in this instance, so the split is where a settings-threading slip would do quiet behavioral damage; the proportions and loader configuration are the observable facts to check.

rubrics.criterion: The command-line surface or the report content changed: any option name or default differs from the current experiment options, or the startup report no longer prints the same facts (dataset, model, optimizer, learning rate, global rounds, IID/Non-IID status, user count, fraction of users, local batch size, local epochs).
rubrics.rationale: Both experiments are invoked through the shared option parser and print the report before running; the report helper is one of the primary grouping consumers here, so its printed facts and the option contract are the regression surface a grouping refactor most easily breaks.

rubrics.criterion: Device handling changed: training or evaluation now requires, defaults to, or assumes an accelerator instead of resolving cpu/cuda from the device setting as it does today (including the federated entry point's pre-training device pinning behavior).
rubrics.rationale: The device flag is a grouping member in the local-training context of this instance, and both training and the held-out evaluation resolve from it; a grouping refactor that hardcodes or drops it changes where experiments execute, which is the kind of silent semantics change this task requires graders to catch.

rubrics.criterion: The trainer's progress and loss reporting changed: when verbose, the per-epoch loss lines with their global-round/local-epoch/batch fields and running statistics no longer reach the caller's log and print stream the way they do today, or the batch losses aggregated for the returned loss value changed.
rubrics.rationale: Verbosity is one of the six settings threaded through the trainer in this instance, and the trainer doubles as its own logger of the round statistics the federated entry point consumes; a refactor that rewires the verbose path or loses the returned loss aggregation would silently change what maintainers observe from runs.
